question.worked_solution:
First, we isolate the term with the variable exponent by dividing both sides by $3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}3\cdot {2}^{y} & =24 \\ \frac{3\cdot {2}^{y}}{3} & =\frac{24}{3} \\ {2}^{y} & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we rewrite $8$ as ${2}^{3}$ to get:

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{y} & =8 \\ {2}^{y} & ={2}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since both sides of the equation share the same base $(2)$, we equate the exponents:

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{y} & ={2}^{3} \\ y & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $y=3.$
